Get or set unbound parameters

Source: R/pipeflow.R
pip_set_params.Rd

pip_get_params() returns the current default values of all unbound parameters of a pipeline or view (i.e., parameters bound to another step via ~step_name are excluded). pip_set_params() updates these parameters in all steps that have them, except for locked steps. Steps whose values change are marked as outdated, together with their downstream dependents. Values that are identical() to the stored ones are skipped and don't outdate any step, unless force = TRUE.

Usage

pip_get_params(x, simplify = TRUE)

pip_set_params(
  x,
  params = list(),
  unknown = c("warn", "ignore", "error"),
  force = FALSE,
  scope = c("pipeline", "view"),
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A pipeflow pip or view.

simplify

If TRUE pip_get_params() returns one value per parameter name, otherwise the values of all steps, grouped by name.

params

A named list of parameters to set. One-sided formulas bind parameters to a step, see Binding parameters to steps.

unknown

How to handle undefined params:

  • "warn" (default) signals a warning and sets the remaining parameters,

  • "ignore" does so silently,

  • "error" fails before anything is changed

force

Logical. If TRUE, every step affected by a parameter update is outdated even if the values were identical() to the stored ones.

scope

Defines the scope of steps for the parameter update if x is a view:

  • "pipeline" (default) sets them in all steps of the pipeline that have the param

  • "view" only in the steps of the view (except bindings, see Views and scope)

...

Passed on to the methods of `pip_param_value<-`()

Value

For pip_get_params(), a named list of unbound parameter values; if the same parameter name appears in multiple steps, the first occurrence in pipeline order is returned. With simplify = FALSE, a named list with an element per parameter name, which is a list of the values named by step, e.g. list(x = list(s1 = 1, s2 = 2), y = list(s1 = 3)). For pip_set_params(), the updated pipeline or view, invisibly.

Views and scope

On a view, a parameter name is updated if it appears in one of the view's steps, otherwise it is considered unknown (see unknown). With scope = "pipeline", the value is spread to every unbound step of the whole pipeline, so that all names get the same value, as pip_get_params() assumes. With scope = "view", the update is limited to the steps of the view.

Bindings ignore scope: a one-sided formula binds a param only in the steps of the view. For example, in pip_set_params(v, list(alpha = 5, data = ~load)), alpha is set in the whole pipeline while data is only bound in the steps of v.

Binding parameters to steps

A one-sided formula binds a parameter to the output of a step, e.g. pip_set_params(p, list(model = ~fit)), as in pip_add().

  • The parameter is bound in all selected steps, except for locked steps. To bind it only in certain steps, select them with a view.

  • The bound steps must come after the step that the formula refers to, otherwise an error is signalled and nothing is changed.

  • A relative reference such as ~-1 is not allowed, but ~try(fit) works as in pip_add().

A bound parameter is no longer unbound: pip_get_params() doesn't return it, and pip_set_params() can't change it any more. To unbind or rebind it, replace the step with pip_replace(). A one-sided formula therfore can't be set as value. Give it as a string instead and turn it into a formula in the step, e.g. with stats::as.formula().

Locked steps

Parameters of locked steps are never changed and their state remains unchanged. pip_get_params() still returns them, so if a locked step comes first among the steps that share a parameter name, pip_get_params() keeps returning the locked step's value after the parameter was set. To read the parameters of the unlocked steps only, use a view that excludes the locked ones, pip_get_params(p[!locked]).

An environment (or a reference object such as an R6 object) that was modified in place is identical to the stored one, so setting it again doesn't outdate the step unless force = TRUE.

Storing annotated values

A new value does not simply replace the stored one. For a step whose param currently holds x, the pipeline basically does pip_param_value(x) <- new_value and stores the result. For plain values, this is just new_value. For an annotated object (e.g. a value with units or labels), a method for its class can instead merge new_value into x, so that the annotations survive (see pip_param_value()). Here, the merging follows these rules:

  • All or nothing: the merged values of all affected steps are computed before anything is changed. If a method fails, nothing is set and an error of class pipeflow_set_params_error reports every failure at once.

  • Comparison: the merged value is what is compared with the stored one, so setting a plain value that an annotated object already holds doesn't outdate the step.

See also

pip_param_value() for storing and passing on annotated parameter values.

Examples

p <- pip_new() |>
  pip_add("load", \(n = 10) seq_len(n)) |>
  pip_add("scale", \(x = ~load, factor = 0.5) x * factor)

# See all unbound/adjustable parameters before running
pip_get_params(p) # list(n = 10, factor = 0.5)
#> $n
#> [1] 10
#> 
#> $factor
#> [1] 0.5
#> 
(pip_run(p))
#> info [2026-11-15 19:18:50.970 UTC]: Starting run of pipeflow 'pipe'
#> info [2026-11-15 19:18:50.971 UTC]: Step 1/2 load
#> info [2026-11-15 19:18:50.972 UTC]: Step 2/2 scale
#> info [2026-11-15 19:18:50.972 UTC]: Finished in 0.002 s (2 done, 0 skipped, 0 failed)
#> <pipeflow> pipe (2 steps)
#> -------------------------
#>     step   params depends state                             out
#> 1:  load        n          done             1,2,3,4,5,6,...[10]
#> 2: scale x,factor    load  done 0.5,1.0,1.5,2.0,2.5,3.0,...[10]
#> -------------------------
#> <ready> last run: 2026-11-15 19:18:50 (0.002 s)
#> steps: 2 done

# Updating params marks affected steps (and their dependents) outdated
pip_set_params(p, params = list(n = 5, factor = 2.0))
p
#> <pipeflow> pipe (2 steps)
#> -------------------------
#>     step   params depends    state                             out
#> 1:  load        n         outdated             1,2,3,4,5,6,...[10]
#> 2: scale x,factor    load outdated 0.5,1.0,1.5,2.0,2.5,3.0,...[10]
#> -------------------------
#> <ready> last run: 2026-11-15 19:18:50 (0.002 s)
#> steps: 2 outdated
(pip_run(p))
#> info [2026-11-15 19:18:50.977 UTC]: Starting run of pipeflow 'pipe'
#> info [2026-11-15 19:18:50.977 UTC]: Step 1/2 load
#> info [2026-11-15 19:18:50.978 UTC]: Step 2/2 scale
#> info [2026-11-15 19:18:50.978 UTC]: Finished in 0.001 s (2 done, 0 skipped, 0 failed)
#> <pipeflow> pipe (2 steps)
#> -------------------------
#>     step   params depends state            out
#> 1:  load        n          done      1,2,3,4,5
#> 2: scale x,factor    load  done  2, 4, 6, 8,10
#> -------------------------
#> <ready> last run: 2026-11-15 19:18:50 (0.001 s)
#> steps: 2 done

# Setting the same values again doesn't outdate any step
pip_set_params(p, params = list(n = 5, factor = 2.0))
p
#> <pipeflow> pipe (2 steps)
#> -------------------------
#>     step   params depends state            out
#> 1:  load        n          done      1,2,3,4,5
#> 2: scale x,factor    load  done  2, 4, 6, 8,10
#> -------------------------
#> <ready> last run: 2026-11-15 19:18:50 (0.001 s)
#> steps: 2 done

# Use force = TRUE to outdate the steps anyway
pip_set_params(p, params = list(n = 5, factor = 2.0), force = TRUE)
p
#> <pipeflow> pipe (2 steps)
#> -------------------------
#>     step   params depends    state            out
#> 1:  load        n         outdated      1,2,3,4,5
#> 2: scale x,factor    load outdated  2, 4, 6, 8,10
#> -------------------------
#> <ready> last run: 2026-11-15 19:18:50 (0.001 s)
#> steps: 2 outdated

# Setting a parameter that is not defined in the pipeline yields a warning
# \donttest{
pip_set_params(p, params = list(nope = 1))
#> Warning: Trying to set parameters not defined in the target: nope
# }
# ... which can be silenced or turned into an error
pip_set_params(p, params = list(nope = 1), unknown = "ignore")
try(pip_set_params(p, params = list(nope = 1), unknown = "error"))
#> Error : Trying to set parameters not defined in the target: nope

# Show the values of all steps with simplify = FALSE
d <- suppressWarnings(
  pip_new() |>
    pip_add("s1", \(x = 1, y = 2) x + y) |>
    pip_add("s2", \(x = 3) x)
)
pip_get_params(d, simplify = FALSE)
#> $x
#> $x$s1
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $x$s2
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> 
#> $y
#> $y$s1
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> 

# pip_get_params() includes locked steps; a view can exclude them
pip_lock(p["load"])
pip_get_params(p) # list(n = 5, factor = 2.0)
#> $n
#> [1] 5
#> 
#> $factor
#> [1] 2
#> 
pip_get_params(p[!locked]) # list(factor = 2.0)
#> $factor
#> [1] 2
#> 

# On a view, a value is set in the whole pipeline unless scope = "view"
r <- pip_new() |>
  pip_add("fit", \(alpha = 1) alpha) |>
  pip_add("plot", \(x = ~fit, alpha = 1) c(x, alpha), tags = "rep")
pip_set_params(pip_view(r, tags = "rep"), list(alpha = 5))
r[["params"]] # alpha = 5 in both steps
#> $fit
#> $fit$alpha
#> [1] 5
#> 
#> 
#> $plot
#> $plot$x
#> ~fit
#> <environment: 0x56250f7f2b80>
#> 
#> $plot$alpha
#> [1] 5
#> 
#> 
pip_set_params(pip_view(r, tags = "rep"), list(alpha = 2), scope = "view")
r[["params"]] # alpha = 5 in "fit", 2 in "plot"
#> $fit
#> $fit$alpha
#> [1] 5
#> 
#> 
#> $plot
#> $plot$x
#> ~fit
#> <environment: 0x56250f7f2b80>
#> 
#> $plot$alpha
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> 

# A formula binds a parameter to the output of a step
q <- pip_new() |>
  pip_add("load", \(n = 5) seq_len(n)) |>
  pip_add("fit_mean", \(x = ~load) mean(x)) |>
  pip_add("fit_max", \(x = ~load) max(x)) |>
  pip_add("report", \(model = NA) paste("result:", model)) |>
  pip_add("report_mean", \(model = NA) paste("mean:", model))

# A view selects the steps to bind, here only "report_mean"
pip_set_params(q["report_mean"], params = list(model = ~fit_mean))

# Without a view, the param is bound in all steps that have it unbound
pip_set_params(q, params = list(model = ~fit_max))
q
#> <pipeflow> pipe (5 steps)
#> -------------------------
#>           step params  depends state
#> 1:        load      n            new
#> 2:    fit_mean      x     load   new
#> 3:     fit_max      x     load   new
#> 4:      report  model  fit_max   new
#> 5: report_mean  model fit_mean   new
#> -------------------------
#> <ready> last run: never
#> steps: 5 new
pip_run(q)
#> info [2026-11-15 19:18:51.003 UTC]: Starting run of pipeflow 'pipe'
#> info [2026-11-15 19:18:51.003 UTC]: Step 1/5 load
#> info [2026-11-15 19:18:51.004 UTC]: Step 2/5 fit_mean
#> info [2026-11-15 19:18:51.004 UTC]: Step 3/5 fit_max
#> info [2026-11-15 19:18:51.005 UTC]: Step 4/5 report
#> info [2026-11-15 19:18:51.005 UTC]: Step 5/5 report_mean
#> info [2026-11-15 19:18:51.006 UTC]: Finished in 0.003 s (5 done, 0 skipped, 0 failed)
q[["report", "out"]]
#> [1] "result: 5"
q[["report_mean", "out"]]
#> [1] "mean: 3"
